questions.text: Does the manufacturer publish the full composition of the product?
questions.hint: Look for a complete material list, including binders and surface layers.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer give the full composition of the acoustic material, including fibre type, binders, finishing layers and chemical additives used in panels, linings or acoustic systems?
questions.hint: Needs more detail than 1.1.1: fibres, binders, finishing layers and additives.

questions.text: Was the product manufactured in the same region of the world where it is sold (local/regional production)?
questions.hint: Compare the country of manufacture with the market of the sale page. Answer 'na' only if local production is not possible for this product type.
questions.applicability: if possible for this product type

questions.text: Does the manufacturer publish carbon footprint data (Carbon Footprint)?
questions.hint: Look for a stated CO2e value, an EPD or an LCA summary.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer provide an ISO 14001 environmental management certificate?
questions.hint: Look for an ISO 14001 mention or certificate.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer declare that the acoustic material does not cause dusting or release microparticles or other pollutants during everyday use indoors?
questions.hint: Look for statements about dust, fibre or microparticle release, or emission test results (e.g. indoor air quality labels).

questions.text: Does the manufacturer's website give information about water or energy savings in the production process?
questions.hint: Look for concrete statements or figures about reduced water or energy use.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer state that it holds, or works with suppliers of materials that hold, a European ecolabel or an OEKO-TEX certificate?
questions.hint: Look for OEKO-TEX, EU Ecolabel or equivalent European environmental labels.

questions.text: Are the glues, impregnations, paints or finishing coatings used in the acoustic material free from formaldehyde, PFAS, PVC and other substances considered harmful to human health?
questions.hint: Look for explicit statements of being free from these substances, or emission class labels. Silence is 'unknown'.

questions.text: Can the acoustic material be easily adapted to different types of interiors and changing user needs without losing its acoustic and aesthetic properties?
questions.hint: Look for reusability, relocation or reconfiguration statements, or modular/format options.

questions.text: Is the material a mono-material (100% one material), enabling full mechanical recycling?
questions.hint: Check the composition: a single material type. Composite panels with several layers are 'no'.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer provide information about the recyclability of the product?
questions.hint: Look for recycling instructions or recyclability statements.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer offer circular-economy solutions, such as take-back of used panels, renovation or reprocessing of the material?
questions.hint: Look for take-back programmes, refurbishment or reprocessing offers.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer inform about a packaging policy for orders from an environmental point of view?
questions.hint: Look for statements about recyclable, reduced or plastic-free packaging.

questions.text: Was the acoustic material designed for long-term use in interiors with high intensity of use, such as offices, schools or public spaces?
questions.hint: Look for intended use in high-traffic or public spaces, or durability/wear classes.

questions.text: Does the acoustic material allow modular interior design, limiting waste during fit-out and future changes of the function of the space?
questions.hint: Look for modular systems, replaceable elements or reconfigurable layouts.

questions.text: After the end of use, can the acoustic material be recycled, regenerated or reused in new products?
questions.hint: Look for end-of-life statements about recycling, regeneration or reuse.
